Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:1.hebrew: ככר של הפקר - וכ"ש אי דנפשיה, אלא רבותא קמ"ל דמצי זכי בהפקר לחליה קדושה עילויה:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:1.english: A loaf of ownerless [property] - And all the more so if [it were] his own; rather, he teaches us a novelty, that one can acquire ownerless [property] for sanctity to take effect upon it.

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:2.hebrew: נטלה על מנת לאוכלה - דכיון שהחזיק בו, קנאה. ואם אכלה, מעל לפי כולה, ומשלם להקדש לפי כולה וחומש, שהרי הוציאה לחולין:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:2.english: He took it in order to eat it - For once he took possession of it, he acquired it. And if he ate it, he misused consecrated property for its entire [value], and he pays the Temple treasury according to its entire [value] plus a fifth, for he has removed it to non-sacred status.

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:3.hebrew: אבל נטלה על מנת להורישה לבניו - ואחר כך הקדישה עסקינן, דקודם לכן לא יכול להקדישה:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:3.english: However, [if] he took it in order to bequeath it to his sons - we are dealing [with a case where] he consecrated it afterward, for prior to that he could not consecrate it.

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:4.hebrew: לא מעל אלא לפי טובת הנאה שבה - שאינו משלם להקדש אלא כפי חזקת טובה שנותן לאביו אחד מן הבנים בשביל שמורישה לו, והיינו טובת הנאה:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:1:4.english: He only committed misuse according to the discretionary benefit in it - For he only pays the Temple treasury according to [the value of] the gratitude that one of the sons gives to his father because he bequeaths it to him, and that is [what is meant by] discretionary benefit.

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:2:1.hebrew: ככרי יהא אסור עליך, וחזר ונתנו למודר במתנה, מהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:2:1.english: [If one said,] "My loaf shall be forbidden to you," and then he gave it to the one bound by the vow as a gift, what is [the law]?

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:2:2.hebrew: כי איתיה ברשותיה - כלומר, כל זמן שהוא של מדיר הוא דאסור, דהכי משמע: "ככרי" — כל זמן שהוא שלי:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:2:2.english: When it is in his possession - That is to say, as long as it belongs to the one who makes the vow, that is when it is forbidden; for this is what "my loaf" implies: as long as it is mine.

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:2:3.hebrew: או דלמא עליך א"ל - ועלויה שויתיה לאותו ככר הקדש, ואע"פ שנתנו לו במתנה, אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:2:3.english: Or perhaps "for you" he said to him - And upon him he rendered that loaf consecrated, and even though he gave it to him as a gift, it is forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:3:1.hebrew: אלא - הא קמבעיא ליה: האי דאמר "ככרי עליך", אי אמרי' דכל זמן שהוא ברשותיה, דאי אתי לידיה מיניה דיליה קאמר ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:3:1.english: But - This is what he is asking: [Regarding] this [person] who says, "My loaf [is forbidden] to you," if we say that [it means] as long as it is in his possession — [meaning] that if it comes into his [the other's] hand from him himself, he is saying [that it is forbidden] to him [— then what does "my loaf" come to exclude?]

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:3:2.hebrew: ולאפוקי דאי גנבה מיגנב - לאותו ככר, ונתנה לו הגנב במתנה, שאינו אסור בה הואיל והוא עצמו לא נתנה לו, או דלמא אע"ג דאי גנבה ליה מיגנב, אסירה ליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:3:2.english: And to exclude [a case] where he stole it - [Namely,] that loaf, and the thief gave it to him as a gift, [meaning] that he is not forbidden from [benefiting from] it since he [the owner] himself did not give it to him; or perhaps, even though he stole it from him, it is forbidden to him.

Rashi on Nedarim 34b:3:3.hebrew: לא לאפוקי דאי אזמניה עליה - למיכל מההוא ככר מעיקרא, והדר א"ל "ככרי עליך". דהתם, כיון דאזמניה עליה, קנה חלקו כמה שהוא יכול לאכול הימנה, ואינו יכול לאוסרה עליו, דלאו כוליה דנותן הוא אלא גם דמזומן:
Rashi on Nedarim 34b:3:3.english: No, [it comes] to exclude [a case] where he invited him to [eat] it - to eat from that loaf initially, and afterward he said to him: "My loaf [is forbidden] to you." For there, once he invited him to [eat] it, [the guest] acquired his portion — as much as he is able to eat from it — and [the host] cannot forbid it to him, because not all of it belongs to the giver, but rather [part of it] also belongs to the invited [guest].

Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:1:1.hebrew: היתה לפניו ככר של הקדש וכו' - תימה: אי איירי בהקדש, מאי שייכא כאן מלתא דרבא גבי מתני' דמיירי בקונמות? ונראה דרבא מיירי בקונמות, והקדש דנקט לאו דוקא, אלא כהקדש קאמר. וא"ת: אמאי נקט מלתא בקונמות, כיון דבהקדש מצי למינקט? וי"ל: דבהקדש לא אמרי' "מעל לפי טובת הנאה שבה" אם אין בו שוה פרוטה, דאין מועל בהקדש בפחות משוה פרוטה; אבל בקונמות, בכל דהו איכא איסור הנאה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:1:1.english: "There was before him a loaf of consecrated [property], etc." - [This is] puzzling: if [the Gemara] is speaking of consecrated property, how does Rava's statement apply here, regarding our Mishnah which deals with konamot? It appears that Rava is speaking of konamot, and [the term] "consecrated property" that he used is not meant literally; rather, he meant "like consecrated property." And if you ask: why did he state [his] teaching regarding konamot, since he could have stated it regarding consecrated property? One can answer: regarding consecrated property, we do not say "he has committed misuse according to the discretionary benefit in it" if it does not have the value of a perutah, for one does not commit misuse of consecrated property for less than the value of a perutah; whereas regarding konamot, there is a prohibition of benefit for any amount whatsoever.

Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:1:2.hebrew: ואמר ככר זו הקדש - בלשון זה אמר: אע"פ שלא אמר "לכשאזכה בה", אפ"ה כי זכה בה הוי הקדש, והואיל ודעתו לזכות בה. וא"ת: והא אין אדם מקדיש דשלב"ל, ולא דמי לאומר "הרי פסח קדושה לאחר שלשים" דהויא קדושה — התם בידו להקדיש מיד, אבל הכא לאו בידו להקדיש מיד! לכ"נ שנטלה וזכה בה ולאח"כ הקדישה, ובא אדם אחר ונטלה ואכלה — או הוא עצמו מתחילתו שזכה בה נטלה לאוכלה — זכה בכולה, והלכך הקדש נמי חל על כולה, ולכך מעל לפי כולה; ואם מתחלת נטילתה לזכות בה בכולה להוריש לבניו, לחלוק להם או ליתנה למי שירצה — ואין לו בה אלא טובת הנאה, אבל גוף הדבר אינו שלו, והקדש כמו כן, שהרי אין אדם מקריב אלא מה שיש לו בה, ולכך מעל לפי טובת הנאה שבה. ול"נ, דלישנא דרבא לא משמע הכי; דקאמר "ככר זה הקדש", ואחר מכאן "נטלה לאוכלה" — משמע דהאי אחר שהקדיש, שלא זכה בה עני אחר מכיון שהקדישה. לכ"נ דלעולם לא זכה בה עדיין בשעת הקדש. וכי תימא: אין אדם מקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם, ועדיין לא זכה בה — מיירי שהוא בתוך ארבע אמותיו, וארבע אמות שלו קנו לו; אי נמי, כיון שבידו לזכות בה, שהוא קרוב ממנה יותר משום אדם, הוי חשיב שפיר דבר (שלא) בא לעולם, כדאמר פרק האומר בקידושין (דף סב -): כל שבידו לאו כמחוסר מעשה דמי. נטלה לאכלה — כלומר: אחר שזכה בה והקדישה כדפרישית, שהיתה תוך ארבע אמותיו והקדישה אחר מכאן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:1:2.english: "And he said: This loaf is consecrated" - He spoke using this formulation: even though he did not say "when I acquire it," nevertheless, once he acquires it, it becomes consecrated, since his intent was to acquire it. And if you ask: But a person cannot consecrate something that has not yet come into the world, and this is not comparable to one who says, "Behold, [a] Passover [offering] is consecrated after thirty [days]," where it becomes consecrated — [for] there it is in his power to consecrate immediately, whereas here it is not in his power to consecrate immediately! Therefore, it appears that he took it and acquired it and afterwards consecrated it, and another person came and took it and ate it — or he himself, when he initially acquired it, took it to eat it — [so] he acquired all of it, and therefore the consecration also takes effect on all of it, and therefore he misused [consecrated property] based on its entire value. And if from the beginning of his taking it [his intent was] to acquire it in its entirety to bequeath to his sons, to divide among them or to give it to whomever he wishes — he has in it only the benefit of discretion, whereas the substance of the item is not his, and consecration is likewise [limited], for a person only offers [to the Temple] what he has in it, and therefore he misused [consecrated property] based on the benefit of discretion that is in it. However, this is not plausible, for Rava's wording does not imply this; for he says, "This loaf is consecrated," and afterwards, "he took it to eat it" — which implies that this [taking] was after he consecrated [it], [meaning] that another poor person did not acquire it once he consecrated it. Therefore, it appears that indeed he had not yet acquired it at the time of consecration. And if you say: A person cannot consecrate something that has not yet come into the world, and he had not yet acquired it — [the Gemara] is speaking of a case where it is within his four cubits, and his four cubits acquired it for him; alternatively, since it is in his power to acquire it, as he is closer to it than any [other] person, it is properly considered something that has (not) [i.e., has] come into the world, as [the Gemara] states in chapter HaOmer in Kiddushin (62a): Anything that is in his power is not considered lacking an act. "He took it to eat it" — that is to say, after he acquired it and consecrated it, as I explained, that it was within his four cubits and he consecrated it afterwards.

Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:1:3.hebrew: נטלה לאוכלה מעל לפי כולה - לפי שנתכוון לשנות כולה מרשות הקדש, ולכך מעל לפי כולה. נטלה ע"מ להורישה לבניו — א"כ לא נתכוון לשנות בכולה, ולכך לא מעל אלא לפי טובת הנאה. ומידי דהוה אמשאיל קרדום של הקדש ובקע בו — לא מעל אלא לפי טובת הנאה שבה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:1:3.english: [If] he took it to eat it, he committed misuse based on its entire [value] - Because he intended to remove all of it from the domain of consecrated property, therefore he committed misuse based on its entire [value]. [If] he took it in order to bequeath it to his sons — if so, he did not intend to remove all of it, and therefore he committed misuse only based on the discretionary benefit. And it is analogous to one who lends a consecrated axe and [the borrower] chops with it — he committed misuse only based on the discretionary benefit in it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:2:1.hebrew: או דלמא עליך אמר ליה ועילויה דידיה שוויה הקדש - לפי גירסא זו דייק מלשון "עליך", וקשה: דא"כ מאי פריך בסמוך מ"פרה שאני נהנה לך" — הא לא אמר ליה "עליך"! הא ליכא למימר דבסמוך פריך מ"נכסי עליך וכו'", דהא מדגרסינן בסיפא "או שניתנה לו במתנה", ולא קתני "שנתנה לו", משמע דאפרה קאי ולא אנכסים. לכ"נ דגרס הכא: "או דלמא עילוייה שויי' הקדש", בלא "עליך": אמר ליה: פשיטא דאע"ג דמהני במתנה — אסור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:2:1.english: "Or perhaps he said 'upon you' to him, and rendered it consecrated with respect to him." - According to this reading, [the Gemara] infers [this] from the wording "upon you" [aleikha], and this is difficult: for if so, why does [the Gemara] object shortly [afterward] from [the case of] "a cow from which I derive benefit [is konam] to you" — [there] he did not say "upon you"! [And] one cannot say that shortly [afterward] it objects from [the clause] "my property [is forbidden] upon you, etc.," for since we read in the latter clause "or if it [fem.] was given to him as a gift," and it does not teach shenatnah lo, it implies that it refers to the cow [which is feminine] and not to the property [which is plural]. Therefore, it appears [to us] that the reading here is: "Or perhaps he rendered it consecrated upon him," without "upon you." [The Gemara continues:] He said to him: It is obvious that even though it is effective as a gift, it is forbidden.

Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:3:1.hebrew: אלא לאפוקי מאי לאפוקי דאי גנבה מיגנב אמר ליה לאפוקי דאי אזמניה עליה - הכי גריס ר"ת, וה"פ: פשיטא דאסור כי יהבה ליה במתנה, אלא לאפוקי מאי — כלומר: ומה שאסר, לענין מה אסרה עליו? וכי תעלה על דעתך לומר שאסרה עליו לענין דאי גנבה מיגנב? זהו תימה, דלא אסרה עליו אלא כשבא לידו בגניבה, דאין זו סברא לומר דאסיק אדעתיה דמיגנבא. וכן צ"ל ע"כ, דאי ס"ד דבמתנה מותרת, הא ודאי כל זמן שבידו לא הוצרך לאוסרה, דבע"כ לא יקחנה, וצ"ל דלענין גניבה אסרה עליו, וזהו תימה כדפי'. ומשני: דאי אזמניה עליה — זה בא לאוסרה עליו, דמזה אסיק אדעתיה שפיר, ולעולם אימא לך דבמתנה מותרת. ואע"ג שדחה סברא פשיטותא, מ"מ רבא במילתיה, דאמר רבא דאסור על ידי מתנה, ולהכי פריך ליה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 34b:3:1.english: "Rather, to what [case does it] apply? To [a case] where he steals it? He said to him: To [a case] where he invited him [to eat] of it" - This is how Rabbeinu Tam reads [the text], and this is its explanation: [Rava said:] "It is obvious that it is forbidden when he gives it to him as a gift." [Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin asked:] "Rather, to what [case does it] apply?" — that is to say, [in] that which he forbade [it], with respect to what [case] did he forbid it to him? Would you think to say that he forbade it to him for [the case] where he steals it? That is astonishing, that he only forbade it to him when it comes into his hand through theft, for it is not logical to say that it entered his mind that it would be stolen. And so one must say perforce, for if you should think that in [the case of] a gift it is permitted, why, certainly as long as it is in his [own] hand he did not need to forbid it, for against his will he would not take it [anyway], and one would have to say that he forbade it to him with respect to theft — and that is astonishing, as I explained. And he answers: "[It applies] where he invited him [to eat] of it" — this [vow] comes to forbid it to him [in that case], for of this it did indeed enter his mind, and in truth I can tell you that in [the case of] a gift it is permitted. And even though he refuted [Rava's] "obvious" reasoning, nevertheless Rava [stands] by his statement — for Rava said that it is forbidden via a gift — and therefore [the Gemara] objects to him [in the following passage].
